result.topic_en: Euler expresses the frictional retardation in a tube in terms of its cross-section with a single empirical coefficient, explains that the wall pressure (state of compression) must be found to determine friction, and sets up the problem of a vessel kept full draining through a variable tube ABMNCD.

items.quote: Ad effectum igitur frictionis, quouis caſu determinandum, preſſionem inueſtigari oportet, quam aqua vbique in latera exerit: ſeu ſtatus compreſſionis aquae in ſingulis tubi locis definiri debet.
items.english: Therefore, to determine the effect of friction in any case, one must investigate the pressure which the water exerts everywhere on the sides; that is, the state of compression of the water at each place in the tube must be defined.

items.quote: hanc inueſtigationem, more apud Analyſtas ſolito, inſtitui debere, ita vt quantitates incognitae in calculo tanquam cognitae tractentur.
items.english: This investigation must be carried out in the manner usual among analysts, so that unknown quantities are treated in the calculation as if known.

items.quote: Sit igitur vas ſuperne in AB perpetuo aqua plenum, ſiue quod amplitudo AB ſit infinita, ſiue quod continuo ſufficiens aquae copia affluat. Infra autem hoc vas deſinat in tubum, vel canalem ABMNCD, tam figurae, quam amplitudinis vtcunque variabilis, per quem aqua defluat, in eiusque orificio CD erumpat.
items.english: Let a vessel be kept always full of water at AB, either because the width AB is infinite or because a sufficient supply of water continually flows in. Below, the vessel ends in a tube or channel ABMNCD, of arbitrarily variable shape and width, through which water flows down and bursts out at its orifice CD.

items.quote: Etiamſi motus aquae, cum primum fluere inceperit, acceleratur, tamen mox ad motum vniformem redigetur, quo deinceps continuo fluere perget.
items.english: Although the motion of the water is accelerated when it first begins to flow, it will soon be reduced to a uniform motion, with which it will thereafter continue to flow.
